newsitem.title: USA: Transocean sees Q2 EPS $0.10 below estimate.
newsitem.headline: Transocean sees Q2 EPS $0.10 below estimate.

text.p: Transocean Offshore Inc said Thursday it expected second-quarter earnings to be $0.10 a share lower than analysts' projections because of contract and repair delays.
The company did not put a dollar amount on its second-quarter earnings and did not give industry analysts' projections.
A May 1 First Call consensus estimate of 21 brokers put Transocean's second-quarter earnings at $0.65 a share.
The company earned $0.74 per share in the second quarter of last year, according to First Call.
The offshore drilling company attributed the lower-than-expected earnings to delays in starting contracts with its Discover Seven Seas and Offshore Amirante rigs.
Transocean also cited higher spending on the Discover and two North Sea semisubmersibles, which completed scheduled shipyard stays during the quarter.

Transocean's chief executive Michael Talbert said in a statement labor shortages at ship yards and lenghtening delivery schedules for rig components caused delays in the completing the company's upgrade programs.
Talbert said the company continued to see "strengthening conditions in the offshore drilling market."
"We fully expect drilling activity levels in the deepwater and harsh environment segments of the offshore industry to remain strong," Talbert said.
Transocean said Thursday it received contracts for four of its rigs.

Gulf of Suez Petroleum Co contracted two jackups for two years for $12.8 million per rig in the first year and $13.5 million per rig in the second year, the company said. It added drilling will start when existing contracts with Gulf of Suez end in early October.

The company also said it expected to sign a one-year contract with Enron Oil & Gas Co and Gas India Ltd in August. Transocean said it expected $22.6 million in revenues from the contract, which would start in Decmeber.

Finally, Transocean said Atlantic Richfield Co's Arco Qatar and Pennzoil Co's Pennzoil Qatar Inc each contracted for a combined 230 days starting mid-July. The company added it expected the contracts to generate a total of $9.8 million in revenues.
Transocean's stock traded at $74 Thursday morning, down 1-3/8.
